status: draft: candidate statements on AI and the social contract, to be coded by blind readers for every voice and then chosen by the instrument checks (scripts/instrument_check.py)
drafted: 2026-11-03, by Claude at Benjamin's direction: make the survey representative of policy, labour, civil-rights, faith, whistleblower and attention-economy voices

candidates.proposition: Over the next decade, AI will eliminate more jobs than it creates.
On its current course, advanced AI will concentrate wealth and power in a small number of companies.
Technology built to capture people's attention has seriously harmed mental health and social life.
AI-generated content is a serious threat to a society's shared sense of what is true.
An AI can be a genuine friend or companion to a person.
Work gives people dignity and purpose that an income alone cannot replace.
Some parts of human life, such as raising children, art or worship, should be kept free of AI.
Companies competing for profit cannot be trusted to make AI safe on their own.
AI companies that train on people's writing, art or data owe them permission or payment.
Large inequality created by AI is acceptable as long as everyone ends up better off.
Workers should have a legal say in how AI is used in their workplaces.
Antitrust law should be used to break up or restrain the largest AI and technology companies.
Employees of AI companies should be legally protected when they warn the public about risks.
US states should be free to pass their own AI laws rather than wait for one national standard.
The law should restrict children's use of AI companion chatbots.
Governments should build publicly owned AI systems as public infrastructure.
As AI advances, people should receive a guaranteed income that is not tied to work.
AI systems should never be allowed to decide on their own to use lethal force.
Governments should be barred from using AI for mass surveillance of their own citizens.
